title: Expression and purification of GST-tagged Kai proteins
author: Anika Wiegard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.48ggztw
materials: enzymatic lysis by lysozyme: resuspend cells in 15 ml ice-cold extraction buffer [50 mM Tris/HCl (pH8), 150 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, 1 mM DTT (only for KaiC proteins: 5 mM MgCl 2 , 1 mM ATP) ] . For this resuspend pellet thoroughly in 5 ml buffer using a paint brush or pasteur pipette. Then add the remaining 10 ml buffer and mix well without creatung foam add a spatula tip’s worth of lysozyme (or add lysozyme stock solution to a final concentration of 1mg lysozyme ml -1 ) add 125 U benzonase incubate on ice for 30 min. Optional: mix every 5 min or place on a magnetic stirrer Note: you can skip enzymatic lysis step and perform longer sonication instead 00:30:00, incubation on ice Benzonase Merck Millipore (EMD Millipore) Catalog #101654

steps.title: Transform expression cells
steps.instruction: Transform E. coli expression strain (e.g., BL21) with the pGEX‑6P1‑based expression plasmid.

steps.title: Prepare overnight pre‑culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 100 mL Terrific Broth (Carl Roth Cat.# X972.2) containing 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin; incubate 16–18 h at 37 °C, 200–250 rpm.

steps.title: Inoculate large expression culture
steps.instruction: Transfer the pre‑culture into 1 L Terrific Broth with 100 µg mL⁻¹ ampicillin in an Erlenmeyer flask of at least 2 L capacity; incubate at 37 °C, 200–250 rpm.

steps.title: Induce protein expression
steps.instruction: For KaiC: grow without IPTG at 37 °C for ~72 h (leaky promoter yields soluble protein). For KaiA or KaiB: grow 3 h at 37 °C, add IPTG to a final concentration of 1 mM, then continue incubation at 37 °C, 200–250 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture 10 min at 4 °C, 4000 g; discard supernatant and keep the cell pellet on ice.

steps.title: Lyse cells by sonication
steps.instruction: Sonicate the cell suspension on ice for 6 min using a Bandelin Sonopuls homogenizer, keeping the temperature below 15 °C. If no enzymatic lysis was performed, use an alternative protocol: 10 s pulse/10 s pause for 25 min at 30 % output.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate 20 min at 4 °C, 23000 g; retain the supernatant (soluble proteins) on ice. If conical tubes cannot withstand 23000 g, reduce the speed and increase the time accordingly.

steps.title: Equilibrate glutathione resin
steps.instruction: Swirl the stock of Glutathione Agarose 4B (Macherey‑Nagel Cat.# 745500.10) or Glutathione Sepharose 4B (GE Healthcare); transfer 1 mL to a 50 mL conical tube, add 5–10 mL extraction buffer, centrifuge 4 min at 1500 g, 4 °C, and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Bind protein to resin
steps.instruction: Add the soluble protein (step 7) to the equilibrated resin; rotate overhead for at least 20 min at room temperature (e.g., IntelliMixer program F1 at 5 rpm). Incubation may be extended up to 3 h.

steps.title: Pellet resin after binding
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the resin 4 min at 1500 g, 4 °C; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash resin
steps.instruction: Perform four successive washes:

substeps.instruction: Add 45 mL ice‑cold extraction buffer, mix thoroughly, centrifuge 4 min at 1500 g, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Repeat the above wash three more times (total of four washes).

steps.title: Transfer resin to prescission buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL ice‑cold prescission buffer (50 mM Tris/HCl pH 8, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM DTT; for KaiC additionally 5 mM MgCl₂ and 1 mM ATP) to the resin, transfer the pellet to a 2 mL reaction tube, centrifuge 4 min at 1500 g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, and repeat until all resin is transferred. Use extraction buffer instead of prescission buffer if the GST tag will not be cleaved.

steps.title: Overnight protease cleavage
steps.instruction: Mix the resin with 500 µL ice‑cold prescission buffer, add 12.5 µL PreScission protease (GE Healthcare Cat.# 27084301), and incubate overnight at 4 °C with constant rotation (IntelliMixer program F4 at 5 rpm). Skip this step if the GST‑tagged protein will be eluted directly.

steps.title: Collect cleavage eluates
steps.instruction: For each of five sequential eluations, centrifuge the resin 4 min at 1500 g, 4 °C and transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube (eluate 1‑5).

steps.title: Elute GST‑tagged protein
steps.instruction: Prepare glutathione solution: 40 mM reduced L‑glutathione, 50 mM Tris, adjust pH 8 with NaOH; for KaiC add 5 mM MgCl₂ and 1 mM ATP. Elution 1: add 1 mL solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature with rotation (IntelliMixer program F4 at 5 rpm), centrifuge 4 min at 1500 g, 4 °C, collect supernatant. Elutions 2‑5: add 500 µL solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature with rotation, centrifuge as above, and collect each supernatant.

steps.title: Bradford analysis of fractions
steps.instruction: For each collected fraction, mix 80 µL Bradford reagent with 5–20 µL fraction in a 96‑well plate; a blue colour indicates protein presence. Optionally assess purity by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Buffer exchange of pooled protein
steps.instruction: Combine all high‑quality eluate fractions, transfer to a disposable centrifugal concentrator (choose appropriate molecular‑weight cut‑off), concentrate by centrifugation, add the desired final buffer, reconcentrate; repeat until the buffer is completely exchanged. Follow the manufacturer’s recommendations for centrifugal force. Ensure removal of glutathione unless further anion‑exchange chromatography is not required.

steps.title: Set up anion‑exchange chromatography
steps.instruction: Connect a 10 mL sample loop to the system, install a MonoQ (1 mL) or ResourceQ (1 mL) column, replace ethanol in capillaries and the loop with water, then wash the column with at least 10 column volumes of degassed MilliQ water (flow ≤1 mL min⁻¹). Prepare eluent A and eluent B as described for Kai proteins.

steps.title: Equilibrate chromatography column
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the column with at least 10 column volumes of buffer A; keep the flow rate ≤1 mL min⁻¹. Equilibration may be performed overnight at a lower flow rate if desired.

steps.title: Optional system test run
steps.instruction: Run the programmed method without injecting a sample and monitor absorbance at 280 nm (and at 220 nm if the instrument allows simultaneous detection).

steps.title: Protein purification by anion exchange
steps.instruction: Dilute the protein in 10 mL eluent A, load onto the sample loop (set injection valve to load), run the chromatography program, monitor absorbance at 280 nm (and 220 nm if possible), and collect fractions of 0.5 mL or 1 mL.

steps.title: Bradford analysis of chromatography fractions
steps.instruction: For each collected fraction, mix 5–20 µL fraction with 80 µL Bradford reagent in a 96‑well plate; a blue colour confirms protein presence. Keep desired fractions and evaluate homogeneity by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Final buffer exchange (if needed)
steps.instruction: Concentrate the selected fractions in a centrifugal concentrator, add the desired final buffer, reconcentrate, and repeat until the buffer is fully exchanged. Choose the molecular‑weight cut‑off and centrifugal force according to the concentrator manufacturer’s instructions; use the Kai‑protein buffers listed for the intended application.
